title: Beyond the 956: Walter Koenig, 'Star Trek's' original Chekov, dies at 90
excerpt: Walter Koenig, the actor best known as Ensign Pavel Chekov on the original "Star Trek" series, has died at 90. He died Sunday, October 25, 2026, at his home in North Hollywood, according to his representative.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Walter Koenig, the actor best known as Ensign Pavel Chekov on the original "Star Trek" series, has died at 90.

Koenig died on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at his home in North Hollywood, with his daughter, Danielle, and his niece by his side, according to a statement from his representative. His representative said he died of old age. Variety also confirmed his death.

Born Walter Marvin Koenig on September 14, 1936, in Chicago, Illinois, to Russian Jewish immigrant parents, Koenig did not set out to act until after college. He joined "Star Trek" in its second season as Chekov, the young Russian navigator aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise, a character created in part to appeal to younger viewers. His first appearance came in the season two premiere, "The Amok Time," and he went on to play Chekov in 36 episodes of the series.

Chekov became one of the most recognizable members of the Enterprise crew, and Koenig reprised the role in all six films starring the original cast, from "Star Trek: The Motion Picture" in 1979 through "Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country" in 1991, and again in a cameo in "Star Trek Generations." He later returned to the franchise in voice in "Star Trek: Picard" in 2023.

Beyond "Star Trek," Koenig was known to science fiction fans as the telepath Alfred Bester on "Babylon 5," and his credits included "Columbo," "Ironside" and a cameo as himself on "Futurama." He also wrote for television, including an episode of the animated "Star Trek" series, and received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2012. In 2026, he won recognition at the Independent Shorts Awards for his performance in the short film "Mr. Fleischmann."

Koenig was predeceased by his wife, Judy Levitt, who died in 2022, and by his son, Andrew, who died in 2010. He is survived by his daughter, Danielle.

Sources: Statement from the representative of Walter Koenig; Variety; Consequence; TMZ.
